#Text= good-sized onions, cut rather fine; measure about 1/2 cup of sweet

#Text= adding lard gradually until all is used and the meat is golden brown.

#Text= BOILED WATER
#Text=
#Text= It sometimes becomes necessary to boil drinking water, which usually
#Text= has a flat, insipid taste.
#Text=Do young housewives know it is said that
#Text= after water has been boiled and when quite cool if a bottle be half
#Text= filled and shaken well the water will become aerated, and have the
#Text= taste of fresh spring water?

#Text= earthenware or china, never metal.

#Text=VINEGAR MADE FROM STRAWBERRIES
#Text=
#Text= "Aunt Sarah" Landis possessed the very finest flavored vinegar for
#Text= cooking purposes, and this is the way it was made.
#Text=She having a very
#Text= plentiful crop of fine strawberries one season, put 6 quarts of very
#Text= ripe, mashed strawberries in a five-gallon crock, filled the crock
#Text= with water, covered the top with cheese-cloth and allowed it to stand
#Text= in a warm place about one week, when it was strained, poured into jugs
#Text= and placed in the cellar, where it remained six months, perhaps
#Text= longer, when it became very sharp and sour, and had very much the
#Text= appearance of white wine with a particularly fine flavor.
